Getting Started

Getting started with Zinc should feel close to writing plain net/http, just with a tighter routing and request/response API.

Prerequisites

  • Go 1.24+
  • A terminal and a text editor or IDE
  • Comfort with standard Go error handling and modules

Install Zinc

Create a new module and add Zinc: 

mkdir zinc-app && cd zinc-app && \
go mod init example.com/zinc-app && \
touch main.go && \
go get github.com/0mjs/zincmkdir zinc-app && cd zinc-app && ^
go mod init example.com/zinc-app && ^
New-Item -Path . -Name "main.go" -ItemType "file" && ^
go get github.com/0mjs/zinc

Write Your First App

Zinc handlers return error. The simplest startup path is app.Listen(":8080").


main.go 
package main

import (
  "log"

  "github.com/0mjs/zinc"
)

func main() {
  app := zinc.New()

  app.Get("/", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.String("Hello, Zinc!")
  })

  app.Get("/users/:id", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.JSON(zinc.Map{
      "id":   c.Param("id"),
      "path": c.FullPath(),
    })
  })

  log.Fatal(app.Listen(":8080"))
}

Run It

go run .

Then try the routes: 

curl http://localhost:8080/
curl http://localhost:8080/users/42

Add Middleware And Binding

Once the basic app is running, the next step is usually grouped routes plus request binding: 

type CreateUserInput struct {
  Name string `json:"name"`
}

func requestLogger(c *zinc.Context) error {
  log.Printf("%s %s", c.Method(), c.Path())
  return c.Next()
}

func main() {
  app := zinc.New()
  app.Use(requestLogger)

  api := app.Group("/api")
  api.Post("/users", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    var input CreateUserInput
    if err := c.Bind(&input); err != nil {
      return err
    }

    return c.Status(zinc.StatusCreated).JSON(zinc.Map{
      "name": input.Name,
    })
  })
}
